title: Nothing to teach (section 21)
hook: the Tathagata has no teaching to teach; that is called teaching

segments.voice: Yesterday: not the perfect body. The Tathagata isn't finally seen through the body or its marks. Your line: not the body. Did you look again at someone, past how they looked? Day one thousand one hundred thirty-eight.

A grandmother kneels on the kitchen floor, teaching a small child to tie a shoe. Two loops. Cross them. Tuck one under. Pull. After a few tries the child gets it and beams. Now, whose knot is that? The grandmother didn't invent it. Someone taught her, and someone taught them. She's passing on something that was never hers, and the child will pass it on without ever saying her name. Section twenty-one of the Diamond Sutra says something like that about the Buddha's own teaching, and then it goes further. Today: nothing to teach.
screen: `TWO LOOPS, CROSS, TUCK, PULL.` → `WHOSE KNOT IS IT?` → `NEVER HERS TO OWN.`

segments.voice: First, the instruction. The Buddha tells Subhuti: don't imagine that the Tathagata thinks, I have taught a teaching. Don't even form that idea. Second, the warning. Anyone who says the Tathagata has taught a teaching, the Buddha says, is misrepresenting him; such a person, the sutra says, hasn't understood what he teaches. That's startling. This is the voice that has been teaching all through this sutra, and here he refuses the title of the one who taught it. Third, the turn. Why? Because, the sutra says, as for teaching the teaching, there is no teaching to be found that could be taught; and that is what is called teaching the teaching. Set that beside a map. A map is useful. You'd be lost without it. But a map is not the place, and a person who keeps the map and never takes the trip has misunderstood what maps are for. The teaching, in this sutra, is never a possession handed from one owner to another. It's a pointing. Fourth, the question behind. Then Subhuti asks something tender. In ages to come, will there be beings who hear a teaching like this and trust it? The Buddha answers in the sutra's own way: they are not beings, nor are they not beings. The ones who will hear it can't be counted as fixed selves either. The teaching passes through people the way a knot passes through hands. Nobody owns the knot. And yet, every time it's tied right, a shoe stays on. That's the strange humility of section twenty-one. The Buddha teaches, fully and carefully, and then lets go of being the owner of what he taught.
screen: `DON'T THINK: I HAVE TAUGHT.` · `TO SAY SO MISREPRESENTS HIM.` · `NO TEACHING, SO CALLED TEACHING.` · `WILL ANYONE TRUST IT?` · then, large: `NO TEACHING, TEACHING.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice, if you'd like: explain something without owning it. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind one thing you know how to do or understand well: a recipe, a shortcut, a way of calming down, a fact you love. Remember who gave it to you, if you can. Then, in your head, explain it to someone, slowly, as if teaching a friend. Notice if a little pride rides along, the sense of it being yours. Let that pride soften. Finish the explanation as a messenger, not an owner. Then rest with the breath. The bell holds the time.
Nothing to teach. Section twenty-one says there is no teaching to be found that could be taught, and that is called teaching. Today's word.

Your line: no teaching, teaching. Today, when you explain or show someone something, name where you learned it, and hand it over without keeping a claim on it. Day one thousand one hundred thirty-eight.

howItsDone: Some Mahayana teachers frame their own teaching as pointing rather than possessing, and section 21 is read as the Buddha disowning any fixed teaching while still teaching.

fork.setup: someone praises the Buddha for all the teachings he has taught. by section 21, how would the sutra answer?
options: thank them; the teachings are his
say there is no teaching to be found that could be taught
list the teachings one by one
fork.reveal: to say he taught a teaching misrepresents him; there's no teaching to be found, and that is called teaching.

original.note: Sanskrit: the teaching, and also the way things are; Pali dhamma.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Buddha owns a set of teachings he handed out.
what it means: he has no teaching to teach, and that is called teaching; a pointing, not a possession.
what a scholar hears: Subhuti's question about future hearers, answered with 'not beings, nor not beings'; even the hearers are not fixed selves.
